A **finite weighted trellis** has an integer length $T\ge0$. If $T=0$, it is
the empty structure, with no vertex layers, edges, or endpoint weights. If
$T\ge1$, it consists of finite vertex sets $V_1,\ldots,V_T$, edge sets
$E_t\subseteq V_{t-1}\times V_t$ for $2\le t\le T$, positive edge weights
$w_t:E_t\to(0,\infty)$, and initial and terminal weights
$\alpha:V_1\to[0,\infty)$ and $\beta:V_T\to[0,\infty)$. The sets $V_t$ may
be empty. A zero initial or terminal weight disables that endpoint; every edge
in $E_t$ is allowed and has positive weight.

A **path** for $T\ge1$ is a tuple $(v_1,\ldots,v_T)$ with $v_t\in V_t$,
$\alpha(v_1)>0$, $\beta(v_T)>0$, and $(v_{t-1},v_t)\in E_t$ for every
$2\le t\le T$. Its **score** is
$$\alpha(v_1)\left(\prod_{t=2}^{T}w_t(v_{t-1},v_t)\right)\beta(v_T),$$
where the empty product for $T=1$ is $1$. For $T=0$, the unique path is the
empty tuple, with score $1$ (the empty product).

A **prefix path through layer $t$**, for $1\le t\le T$, satisfies the same
conditions through $v_t$, without a terminal-weight condition. For $T=0$,
the empty tuple is the unique prefix path through no layers, with score $1$.
A vertex $v\in V_t$ is **reachable** if some prefix path ends at $v$;
otherwise it is **unreachable**. There are finitely many paths. If at least
one path exists, its maximum score is attained; if none exists, the trellis
has no admissible path.

It exists exactly when $\alpha(v)>0$, and then has score $\alpha(v)=D_1(v)$; when $\alpha(v)=0$ there is no prefix and $D_1(v)=0$.

Fix $t\ge2$ and $v\in V_t$. Every prefix ending at $v$ has a predecessor $u$ with $(u,v)\in E_t$ and is obtained by appending that edge to a prefix ending at $u$. Its score is the predecessor-prefix score multiplied by the positive weight $w_t(u,v)$. By [A1], the best such extension through each $u$ has score $D_{t-1}(u)w_t(u,v)$; if no predecessor prefix exists this value is zero. Taking the maximum over the finite predecessor set, with zero when it is empty, gives exactly the stated recurrence.
The $T=0$ case and the base case in step 1.1, together with the induction step in step 1.2, prove the claim for every trellis length and every layer.

in $E_t$ is allowed and has positive weight.

$\alpha(v_1)>0$, $\beta(v_T)>0$, and $(v_{t-1},v_t)\in E_t$ for every
$2\le t\le T$. Its **score** is
$$\alpha(v_1)\left(\prod_{t=2}^{T}w_t(v_{t-1},v_t)\right)\beta(v_T),$$

one path exists, its maximum score is attained; if none exists, the trellis
has no admissible path.

For a finite weighted trellis with $T=0$, the unique prefix path through no
layers is empty and has score $1$. For $T\ge1$, define $D_1(v)=\alpha(v)$ and,
for $2\le t\le T$,
$$D_t(v)=\max\bigl(\{D_{t-1}(u)w_t(u,v):(u,v)\in E_t\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).$$
Then $D_t(v)$ is the maximum score of a prefix path ending at $v$; if no such
prefix exists, $D_t(v)=0$.

**Input:** A finite weighted trellis and a total order on each vertex set.

**Output:** “No admissible path,” or an admissible path and its score.

If $T=0$, return the empty path with score $1$. Otherwise perform the following
steps:

1. Set $D_1(v)=\alpha(v)$ for all $v\in V_1$. For each layer $t=2,\ldots,T$ and
   each $v\in V_t$, compute
   $$D_t(v)=\max\bigl(\{D_{t-1}(u)w_t(u,v):(u,v)\in E_t\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).$$
   If $D_t(v)>0$, store as $p_t(v)$ the first predecessor $u$ in the supplied
   vertex order attaining this maximum; if $D_t(v)=0$, leave $p_t(v)$
   undefined.
2. Compute $Q(v)=D_T(v)\beta(v)$ for all $v\in V_T$. If every $Q(v)=0$,
   return “no admissible path.”
3. Otherwise choose the first $v_T$ in the supplied order maximizing $Q(v)$,
   and follow the stored pointers $p_T(v_T),p_{T-1}(v_{T-1}),\ldots,p_2(v_2)$
   backwards. Return the resulting path and its score $Q(v_T)$.

The stored predecessor at each layer is a **backpointer**. Following these
pointers backward from a maximizing terminal vertex is called **traceback**.
The given orders make the returned path deterministic when several paths have
the same maximum score. The empty path at $T=0$ is the unique path and is
therefore the unique maximum-score output in that case.

derivations.claim: If $T=0$, [F1] gives the unique empty path and its score $1$, which the branch in [F3] returns. If $T\ge1$, [F2] shows that every positive $D_t(v)$ is attained by a prefix path and a zero value means there is no such prefix. Therefore, for each terminal vertex $v$, $D_T(v)\beta(v)>0$ exactly when some full path ends at $v$; when positive it is the largest score of such a path.

Suppose $T\ge1$. The finite set of terminal values has a positive maximum exactly when at least one full path exists. If it is positive, let $v_T$ be the maximizing terminal vertex; then $D_T(v_T)>0$ and $\beta(v_T)>0$. If $T=1$, then $D_1(v)=\alpha(v)$ and $Q(v)=\alpha(v)\beta(v)$, so the selected one-vertex tuple $(v_1)$ is already an admissible path of maximum score; no backpointer is needed. If $T\ge2$, then by [F3], $p_T(v_T)$ is defined and selects an allowed edge from some $v_{T-1}$ with $D_{T-1}(v_{T-1})w_T(v_{T-1},v_T)=D_T(v_T)>0$, so $D_{T-1}(v_{T-1})>0$ because the edge weight is positive. In the $T\ge2$ case, repeating this argument for the layers $t=T,T-1,\ldots,2$ shows every pointer is defined, each selected pair is an allowed edge, and the chain ends at $v_1$ with $D_1(v_1)=\alpha(v_1)>0$. The chain is therefore a path, and its score is $D_T(v_T)\beta(v_T)$, the maximum terminal value from step 1.1. If all terminal values are zero, step 1.1 shows there is no path, so the algorithm correctly returns “no admissible path.” The $T=0$ case is settled by step 1.1.

The $T=0$ branch takes constant time. For $T\ge1$, each vertex is initialized or scanned a bounded number of times, each edge contributes one candidate product and comparison, and traceback visits at most $T$ layers. Thus the time is $O(1+T+V+E)$. The algorithm stores at most one backpointer per vertex and scores for the current and preceding layers, so auxiliary storage is $O(1+V)$.

$$p(z,y)=\pi(z_1)B(z_1,y_1)\prod_{t=2}^{T}A(z_{t-1},z_t)B(z_t,y_t).$$
The **evidence** of $y$ is $p(y)=\sum_{z\in S^T}p(z,y)$. When $p(y)>0$,
the conditional path mass is $p(z\mid y)=p(z,y)/p(y)$, and a
**sequence MAP (maximum-a-posteriori) path** is any $z$ maximizing this conditional mass. If $p(y)=0$,
the conditional path mass is undefined, so there is no posterior sequence MAP
path for that observation sequence. A zero transition or emission factor gives
that hidden path zero joint mass.

**Input:** A finite discrete HMM $(S,Y,\pi,A,B)$, an observation sequence
$y=(y_1,\ldots,y_T)\in Y^T$ with $T\ge1$, and a total order on $S$.

1. Form a trellis with $V_t=S$ at every layer. Set
   $\alpha_y(s)=\pi(s)B(s,y_1)$ and terminal weights $\beta_y(s)=1$.
2. For every $t=2,\ldots,T$, include the edge $(r,s)$ exactly when
   $A(r,s)>0$ and $B(s,y_t)>0$, and give it weight
   $w_t(r,s)=A(r,s)B(s,y_t)$.
3. Run [[alg-viterbi-max-product-on-finite-trellis]] on this trellis using the
   supplied state order. If it returns no admissible path, return
   “zero evidence; no conditional sequence MAP.” Otherwise return its path as
   the decoded hidden-state sequence.

Zero transition or emission factors are omitted from the trellis, so every
trellis path has positive joint mass.

Given a finite discrete HMM and an observation sequence of positive length, the
sequence-decoding algorithm returns no conditional MAP path exactly when the
observation evidence is zero. When the evidence is positive, it returns a
hidden-state sequence maximizing the posterior probability of the entire
sequence, including when there are ties.
